items.title: Try a 10 to 20 minute walk after dinner
items.text: Walking after a meal is linked to a smaller rise in sugar, with the biggest difference seen when walking 10 to 19 minutes after dinner. In one program, walking after dinner was linked to a rise about 18.3 mg/dL smaller in sugar.

items.title: Keep dinner early
items.text: Eating dinner at 8 pm or later is linked to a rise in sugar, with a difference of about 9.2 mg/dL more. It's a good idea to avoid eating late dinners to keep sugar levels in check.

items.title: Aim for a 13-hour overnight break
items.text: Fasting overnight for 12.8 hours on average, with most nights reaching 13 hours, is a habit that may be linked to sugar levels. In one program, adding an overnight fast to coaching changed sugar levels, but more research is needed to understand the link.
